name: SCAMPER Method
description: Activity-based creative thinking process using seven prompted operations: Substitute, Combine, Adjust, Modify, Put to other uses, Eliminate, Reverse. Developed by Bob Eberle (1971), inspired by Alex Osborn's checklist in Applied Imagination.

steps.name: Substitute (analogy) — What can be substituted?
steps.description:
Come up with another topic that is equivalent to the present topic.

Substitution uses analogy to find equivalent replacements for components, materials, processes, or people. Per Osborn's original checklist: What other material? What other process? What other approach? What other ingredient? What other power source?

Identify elements that can be replaced with alternatives serving the same function, drawn from the same or different domains.

SearchMemories.reason: Find analogous components, materials, or processes in the knowledge graph that could serve as substitution candidates

stop_conditions: At least 3 substitution candidates identified for key components
Each substitution assessed for equivalence to the original
Analogies from other domains considered per Osborn's checklist
next_actions: Add information through convergence in the Combine step

steps.name: Combine (convergence) — What can be combined?
steps.description:
Add information to the original topic through convergence.

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Combination uses convergence — merging separate elements, ideas, or approaches to add new information to the original topic. What ideas, materials, features, processes, or people can be merged? What synergies emerge from combining unlike elements?

Explore both obvious and non-obvious pairings. What happens when you blend approaches, unite resources, or merge features into a single unified whole?

SequentialThinking.reason: Systematically explore convergent combinations between disparate elements to add new information to the original topic
focus_areas: What separate features or ideas can be merged into one unified whole?
What approaches can be blended or used simultaneously?
What unlike elements converge to create new value when combined?

stop_conditions: At least 3 combination ideas generated through convergence
Both obvious and non-obvious pairings explored
Synergies and conflicts between combined elements assessed
next_actions: Identify ways to construct more flexibly in the Adjust step

steps.name: Adjust — What can be adjusted?
steps.description:
Identify ways to construct the topic in a more flexible and adjusted material.

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Adjustment seeks flexibility — finding ways to make the construction of the topic more adaptable, more responsive to different conditions, or better fitted to its context. What can be fine-tuned, calibrated, or made more elastic?

How can the fit between the idea and its environment be improved? What constraints can be loosened to allow adjustment?

SequentialThinking.reason: Systematically explore ways to construct the topic in a more flexible and adjusted form, per Eberle's Adjust operation
focus_areas: What aspects can be made more flexible or adjustable?
How can the topic be constructed for better fit to its context?
What constraints can be loosened to allow flexible adjustment?

SearchMemories.reason: Find prior solutions or patterns in the knowledge graph that demonstrate flexible construction or adjustment techniques

stop_conditions: At least 2 adjustment opportunities identified for flexibility or fit
Each adjustment assessed for how it improves adaptability of the material
Trade-offs between flexibility and stability considered
next_actions: Explore creative changes to scale and emphasis in the Modify step

steps.name: Modify, Magnify, Minify — What can be changed in scale or emphasis?
steps.description:
Creatively change the topic or make a feature or idea bigger or smaller.

Modification operates on scale and emphasis. Magnify: what can be made larger, stronger, higher, longer, thicker, more frequent, or more valuable? Minify: what can be made smaller, lighter, shorter, thinner, less frequent, or more streamlined?

What attributes can be altered? What happens when you change the proportions, dimensions, or emphasis of the topic?

BuildContext.reason: Explore the conceptual neighborhood to identify attributes that could be magnified, minified, or otherwise modified

stop_conditions: Key attributes identified for modification through magnification or minification
At least 2 modifications explored: scale change, emphasis shift, or attribute alteration
Impact of each modification on overall function assessed
next_actions: Identify new scenarios and situations for use in the Put to Other Uses step

steps.name: Put to Other Uses (generate/divergence/connect) — How else can this be used?
steps.description:
Identify the possible scenarios and situations where this topic can be used.

Put to other uses applies generative, divergent, and connective thinking to find new applications, contexts, or purposes beyond the original intent. As-is, where else could this be used? Modified, what new purposes does it serve?

What other markets, audiences, problem spaces, or contexts could benefit? What connections to other domains reveal new use cases?

SearchMemories.reason: Search for alternative contexts, use cases, or domains in the knowledge graph where the topic could generate divergent value

stop_conditions: At least 2 alternative use cases identified beyond the original intent
New user segments, application domains, or problem spaces explored
Divergent and generative thinking applied to connect the topic to new scenarios
next_actions: Remove non-valuable elements in the Eliminate step

steps.name: Eliminate — What can be removed?
steps.description:
Remove ideas or elements from the topic that are not valuable.

Elimination strips away the non-essential to improve efficiency or clarity. What components, features, steps, or rules can be removed without losing core value? What would happen if you simplified radically?

What is not necessary? What adds complexity without adding value? What can be omitted entirely?

BuildContext.reason: Map element dependencies to identify which components can be safely removed without breaking core function

stop_conditions: Non-essential elements identified and assessed for removal
Impact of each elimination on core value evaluated
Simplified version articulated with clear rationale
next_actions: Evolve new concepts through reversal in the Reverse step

steps.name: Reverse, Rearrange — What can be reversed or rearranged?
steps.description:
Evolve a new concept from the original concept through reversal or rearrangement.

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Reversal challenges the assumed order, direction, or structure. What if the sequence were reversed? What if roles were swapped? What if cause and effect were inverted? Rearrangement explores alternative configurations of the same elements.

What new concept emerges when you turn the idea inside out, upside down, or back to front?

SequentialThinking.reason: Systematically invert, flip, or rearrange conventional assumptions, sequences, and structures to evolve new concepts from the original
focus_areas: What if the typical process order were reversed?
What assumptions about sequence, hierarchy, or direction can be inverted?
What new concept evolves from rearranging the original elements?

stop_conditions: At least 2 reversals or rearrangements explored
Conventional assumptions explicitly identified and challenged
At least one reversal yields a new concept evolved from the original
next_actions: SCAMPER cycle complete — synthesize best ideas across all 7 operations
Optionally repeat cycle with refined focus on most promising directions
